rule: Young status is an account-level flag (on by default for new accounts) that gives per-attack protection from uncontrolled monsters, scoped by a region flag and lifted per creature type by quest objectives. It ends on time played, first murder-count rise, a skill-total threshold, or an explicit renounce. Death, healing and stuck-escape are tuned for the young. The first errands are a quest chain (one objective and one reward each), a 12-stop escort tour of services, and a 26-skill training chain that opens a short accelerated-gain window. Creation enforces a stat and skill budget, and falls back silently on mismatch.
keep: per-attack protection check, not a wall
one named exception per quest objective, ended by completion
free full heal at a healer on a timer while young
escort chain as a tour of services, one per service
accelerated gain window tied to a training task, cancelled when the task is cancelled
death notice that explains the rules in plain blocks
change: young clock is account-wide and counts deleted characters; Frankendom keeps the counter on the one character ledger
silent stat fallback to 10/10/10 and silent empty skill list: say what happened on screen
profession stat templates sum differently per era file (80 vs 90); match template to client budget or check at load and log
ore task comment says any ore type, check accepts one item id: fix one or the other
welcome timer comment says login too, but only creation starts it
accelerated window has an open TODO on maximum duration: set a cap as data
look_test: Behind one style flag on the existing ring scene: a town square with three idle creatures that turn to face the player and stay still for 60 s, with one small once-a-minute line in the bottom sheet; then one creature engages for a single first-hunt task and a small newcomer tag shows under the name. Compare with the same square where creatures attack on sight. Judge at 375 wide: does the stare read as safe, is the line noticed without covering the screen. Then open the death notice (items back in pack, sent to healer, three blocks of text) and judge one-screen readability.
